visual_action: A slideshow of still images. It begins with a screenshot of a fabricated tweet from "FactPost" claiming Bad Bunny's Super Bowl halftime show had over 135 million viewers. This is followed by a two-panel meme comparing "Super Bowl LX Halftime Shows." The "America's" side features a photo of Bad Bunny with "135+ million viewers," and the "MAGA's" side features a photo of Kid Rock with "10 million viewers." An image of Bad Bunny performing with dancers, flags (including the US and Puerto Rican flags), and fireworks is also shown.

cast.name: Bad Bunny
cast.evidence: Named and shown in multiple photos and on-screen text, representing 'America's' halftime show.

cast.name: Kid Rock
cast.evidence: Shown in a photo on the 'MAGA's' side of a comparative meme.

cast.name: MAGA
cast.evidence: The on-screen text explicitly labels one side of the comparison as 'MAGA's'.

cast.name: FactPost
cast.evidence: Shown as the author of a fabricated tweet with the handle @factpostnews.

on_screen_text.text: Bad Bunny's Super Bowl halftime show was the most-watched halftime performance of all time with over 135 million viewers.

spoken_summary: The video features a Spanish-language song by Bad Bunny playing throughout. The lyrics include lines like "si mañana muero, yo espero que nunca olviden mi rostro" ("if I die tomorrow, I hope they never forget my face"). No other dialogue is present.
audio_music: An upbeat, celebratory reggaeton track by Bad Bunny ("LA MuDANZA") plays throughout the entire video, creating a hype-filled and positive mood associated with the 'America's' side of the comparison.
editing_pacing: A fast-paced slideshow of still images and screenshots.
manipulation_or_satire: The video uses a fabricated tweet, presented as being from a news source called 'FactPost', to make a false claim about Bad Bunny's Super Bowl viewership. This fake tweet is then used as the premise for a satirical meme comparing the supposed popularity of a mainstream artist (Bad Bunny) to a MAGA-aligned artist (Kid Rock), using invented statistics to mock the latter.
central_claim: Mainstream American culture, represented by Bad Bunny, is vastly more popular than the culture associated with the MAGA movement.
intended_effect: To mock the MAGA movement as culturally unpopular and fringe, while celebrating mainstream, diverse culture as the true 'America'.
